title: The Quiet Autopsy Again
premise: Estate lawyer Jonah Joubert, who has quietly solved three deaths the police ruled accidental, is hired to execute the will of Miriam Vasseur, a woman declared legally dead seven years ago. The will cites a diary that keeps being written after her disappearance, and its final entry names a guest at an upcoming thirtieth-anniversary dinner at the Vasseur family estate. As Jonah traces alibis woven three decades earlier around a drowning everyone agreed to forget, he realizes Miriam staged her own vanishing to force the truth into the open, and that she is still alive, watching. At the anniversary dinner, Jonah exposes the killer among her relatives; Miriam surrenders herself for faking her death, choosing justice over inheritance, while Jonah finally accepts that his invisible life must end.
about_author: V. M. Iversen is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years reading other people's last words before writing any of their own. They live in a coastal town where fog is frequent and funerals are well attended.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. A sealed will arrives naming Miriam Vasseur—legally dead since seven years ago—as testator, with Jonah as executor. His instinct is to burn it; instead he files it. Emotional beat: the thrill of an impossible puzzle reawakening a man who buried his gift after his third quiet investigation nearly got him killed.

chapters.title: Inventory of a Missing Woman
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. At the shuttered Vasseur house, Jonah catalogs the estate and finds the diary in a wall safe, its entries continuing two years past Miriam's disappearance. Beat: unease curdling into obsession as he reads a dead woman describing rooms only someone present could know.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Guest List
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The will stipulates one condition: all beneficiaries attend the family's thirtieth-anniversary dinner or forfeit everything. He interviews the four heirs—a brother, a widow, a nephew, a business partner—each rehearsed, each lying about something small. Beat: Jonah mapping the architecture of shared guilt.

chapters.title: What the Drowned Girl Knew
chapters.summary: POV Miriam (diary excerpts). Thirty years ago, teenage Miriam witnessed something at the lake during the first anniversary gathering: her aunt's drowning was not an accident. Beat: terror of a child learning that adults protect each other, not children.

chapters.title: A Detective Who Isn't
chapters.summary: POV Detective Amara Okafor. Okafor, who closed the file on Miriam's disappearance, notices the estate reactivated and pulls the old records, finding Jonah's name attached to three prior 'accidents.' Beat: professional suspicion sharpening into personal curiosity about this quiet lawyer.

chapters.title: Alibi, Thirty Years Old
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Cross-referencing the diary against the original drowning inquest, Jonah finds every heir's alibi corroborates the others'—too perfectly, like testimony rehearsed around a table. Beat: cold clarity that the family built their innocence together, brick by brick.

chapters.title: The Nephew's Debt
chapters.summary: POV Theo Vasseur. The nephew, drowning in gambling debts, tries to sell estate secrets to a tabloid and instead finds Jonah waiting in his car. Beat: desperation; Theo reveals the heirs meet annually on the anniversary date, a ritual they call 'keeping the calendar.'

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Forensic analysis shows the post-disappearance diary pages were written recently, in aged ink, by someone matching Miriam's hand—or trained to imitate it. Beat: vertigo; either Miriam lives, or someone wants the past exhumed badly enough to forge a ghost.

chapters.title: The Widow's Version
chapters.summary: POV Celeste Vasseur. The widowed sister-in-law privately tells Jonah a different story of the drowning night—that Miriam's father orchestrated the cover-up and made them all swear silence. Beat: grief weaponized into confession, but Celeste's own timeline has a hole Jonah doesn't mention.

chapters.title: Okafor Closes In
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. Okafor confronts Jonah with the pattern across his three prior cases and offers a deal: transparency for immunity. Jonah refuses, protecting a source he won't name—the diary itself. Beat: two investigators circling the same truth from opposite sides of the law.

chapters.title: The Lake in Winter
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah dives the drained lakebed with a retired salvage diver and recovers a locked strongbox containing jewelry identified as the drowned aunt's—items the inquest said were never recovered. Beat: dread hardening into proof that the family lied under oath thirty years ago.

chapters.title: Keeping the Calendar
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo breaks, confessing the annual ritual: each year the heirs retell their alibis, refining them, until memory and lie became indistinguishable. He admits he saw Miriam alive once, two years ago, at a ferry terminal—and said nothing. Beat: shame of complicity inherited like property.

chapters.title: Someone Is Reading Over My Shoulder
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. New diary pages appear in Jonah's own hotel room, addressed to him by name, warning that the dinner will be 'the last keeping.' Someone knows his every move. Beat: hunter realizing he is also hunted, and exhilarated despite himself.

chapters.title: The Business Partner's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. The partner, Ruth Adeyemi, kept meticulous books; hidden columns show payments to a private investigator thirty years ago—to find Miriam, not to bury her. Ruth believes Miriam ran because she learned who killed the aunt. Beat: the case splitting open along a fault line Jonah hadn't mapped.

chapters.title: Okafor's Cold File
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. Reopening the aunt's drowning independently, Okafor finds the coroner's notes were altered and traces the alteration to Miriam's late father. She realizes Jonah is right and the department was wrong. Beat: reluctant alliance forming between law and what lies outside it.

chapters.title: The Hole in Celeste's Night
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah confronts Celeste about her missing ninety minutes the night of the drowning; she admits she helped Miriam's father move the body from boathouse to lake—but swears Miriam's father acted alone, and that Miriam saw them both. Beat: pity for a woman who traded her soul for security.

chapters.title: Invitations
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Formal invitations arrive for the anniversary dinner, issued in Miriam's handwriting, including one to Jonah and one to Okafor. The venue: the Vasseur estate, the lake lit with lanterns. Beat: the trap assembling itself, though no one can say who set it.

chapters.title: Thirty Years to the Hour
chapters.summary: POV multiple, interwoven. The dinner begins; toasts are raised; each heir performs their rehearsed innocence while Jonah watches the door. At the stroke of the hour, the lights fail. Beat: held breath, thirty years of silence about to shatter.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Head of the Table
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Lights return: Miriam stands at the table, alive, playing recordings of the heirs' private confessions gathered over years. She names her father's accomplice in the aunt's murder—Celeste—and demands the truth aloud. Beat: catharsis and horror colliding as the room detonates.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: POV Okafor. In the chaos, the guilty party—revealed to be Celeste, who killed the aunt to protect the family secret and later drove Miriam to flee—lunges; Okafor intervenes, arrest follows, and Miriam voluntarily surrenders for faking her death. Beat: justice arriving through both lawful and unlawful doors at once.

chapters.title: Probate of a Living Woman
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Months later, Jonah handles the legal wreckage: the will voided, the estate divided among restitution claims, Miriam sentenced but serene. She thanks him for finishing what she couldn't do alone. Beat: bittersweet accounting—every truth purchased with something irreplaceable.

chapters.title: The Quiet Autopsy
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Jonah closes his practice, leaves his fourth case file labeled and complete on Okafor's desk, and writes his own account—the book we've been reading. Beat: acceptance; invisibility was always a kind of hiding, and survival means stepping into the light, named.
